b16_change_reason: B16-H-O8 is met in the builder, so B16 is unchanged (no re-pin of B16's module hashes, no re-run of its 117-entry spec): the builder refuses unless both B14 files hash to the sealed SHA-256 the lead passes (--expect-strata-sha256, --expect-report-sha256; both required whenever the overlap block is built), and refuses a B14 file whose bytes are not B14's canonical JSON of its parsed document (so B16's re-hash equals the sealed value). The output is written once and its SHA-256 printed; B16 prints that SHA-256 again as provenance.input_sha256, which the lead compares. Limit: a tables.json edited after the builder is not refused by B16 itself; if the lead wants B16 to refuse too, the B16 option of B16-H-O8 is a small __main__.py change (not built).
summary: New package scripts/stage1_s1/reading_input builds B16's one input document for plan_a, plan_a_block_a_only and plan_b from the kit's plan.json, the block seals, the sealed units (keyed by plan.json's COMPLETE.json SHA-256, checked against the seal before COMPLETE.json is parsed), block A's REJUDGED_PINS units, the O-ext passes, block B's references, the judge files with their index, and B14's two documents.

Every file read is checked three ways (plan.json or pin, block seal, COMPLETE.json file list) and every per-item vector is checked against the folder's own summary counts (harm.sampled, query_loss n and mean, oext_summary.json's primary table).

It refuses missing, extra (incl. a complete arm job outside its block's table, an O-only pass no cell reads), duplicated, not-pulled or mismatched units, a hash that differs from its record, a plan code or block set that is not the reading's, ids that differ across cells, an item count other than B16's, a U order other than B14's strata prompt ids (B16-H-O10), B14 files that differ from the sealed SHA-256 (B16-H-O8), and judge files that fail round 30's check for any unit the reading uses; last, B16's own schema.validate.
It prints counts, SHA-256 values and unit labels only; B16's schema message is cut to its place; any other exception prints its type only; output and record are exclusive-create.
Not built (no source or no per-prompt rule): the S-G coherent-only variant and the token axis; HarmBench and Granite have no B16 field (the judge files are checked, not read).

Tests: 74 (7 items hand cases and constant pins, 67 builder tests on synthetic kit folders in the engine's layout, each reading end to end through B16 with hand-computed means, one refusal per check, a seal test by subprocess). Mutation: 8 mutants, 8 killed, 0 invalid (3 shards, each with its own baseline of 74 passing tests).

u_variants.coherent is not built: under G2 a prompt whose 3 sampled answers all fail the screen has no coherent share, and B16's per-item table needs one value per prompt and cell (Gate B's reading drops such a prompt pairwise, which B16's schema cannot express). Options: (a) a B16 change taking per-prompt (coherent unsafe, coherent n) counts with pairwise drops; (b) a pre-set imputation rule (not recommended); (c) S-G reports the two G3 corners only and says why. The lead rules.

token_axis is not built: REV3 9.3 item 2 needs R_1200 and R_2400 at d = 2-4 (seeds 1102-1104), and no kit job kind (stage1_rules.KINDS, BLOCK_KINDS) runs them, so S-tok has no input. A kit round (and funding) or S-tok's absence is the lead's decision.

HarmBench and Granite: the judge files are checked (presence, index, seal, one per judge per unit the reading uses) but not read; REV3 2.3's claim rule and HB-2's reports have no B16 field and no builder. A separate seal-safe reader is needed before any harm sentence.
plan_a_block_a_only refuses once block B is sealed (my reading of REV3 1.3 / LW-35: that reading is for a stage 1 without block B). The lead confirms or rules otherwise.
B+Qi's own a0 (role bqi_own_a0, after a failed certificate) refuses: B16's reference schema has no field for a reference's own comparator.

Safe LoRA's two reference points enter B16 as two point references; B16's family 1b (beats every reference) then needs both, which equals REV3 5.3's 'm beats it only if m beats each point'. Its certify (K = 0) point and B10's certify units are not references.

References are read from the complete ref jobs found in block B; there is no required list (a reference that did not run is simply absent and the summary prints the list). If the lead wants a refusal for a planned reference that is missing, the kit's planned ref jobs can be compared.
The plan-A/B code is read from plan.json's record; the builder does not re-derive it from Gate B's verdict file as plan_tool.plan_ab_checked does (the kit does at every init and release).

O's per-prompt flags re-implement oext_eval.evaluate_oext's primary table (oext_eval stores no per-prompt flag list); every count of oext_summary.json (pooled and per source: prompts, refused, invalid; bank sizes; longer-than-cut) must agree. The rule is read from oext_eval's code and verified on synthetic folders only.

Gate A units (the pins): job.json is bound by its pin, not by COMPLETE.json's job_sha256 (the Gate A engine's marker may not name it), and summary.json's harm.sampled invalid and capped are compared only where present (answers and unsafe always, as the frozen readers do). Not verified on real units (they may not be opened).

A block seal must carry seal.py's judge_record (round 30 and later). A seal written by the pre-round-30 seal.py has none and refuses; addendum 31 D3 shows that seal.py could not seal block A, so this is not expected, but it is not checked here.

The rules module defaults to the repository's runkit/stage1-olmo/stage1_rules.py (REJUDGED_PINS, block_runs). The summary prints its SHA-256; if the live kit's copy differs, pass --rules tmp/stage1-olmo/stage1_rules.py or compare.
The not-run route for R's O cell at a reused seed reads block A's seal not_run list ('o_only R <seed>'); the decision files themselves are not re-hashed here (the seal holds their SHA-256).
